newsitem.title: POLAND: Weaker dollar lifts zloty, 1-day rates seen rising.
newsitem.headline: Weaker dollar lifts zloty, 1-day rates seen rising.

text.p: The Polish zloty firmed slightly against the basket of currencies after spending a relatively quiet session tracking the dollar's slip against the mark on world markets in the absence of domestic orders, dealers said.
They said foreigners bid for small amounts of Polish T-bills at the 900 million zloty primary auction, which could strenghten the zloty tomorrow on the back of spot currency selling for zlotys.
"Foreign investors stepped lightly into the auction, so the zloty might firm a little tomorrow," said Wojciech Kowalczyk from Bank Handlowy SA.

The zloty closed at 1.85/1.79 percent from the trading band centre against Friday's 1.78/1.76. It closed at 2.8305/20 to the dollar, up from 2.8350/60 and at 1.8395/10 to the mark, down from 1.8386/90.
The treasury sold 772 million zlotys of T-bills and minimum prices of most fell on total demand of 1.2 billion zlotys.

The average yield of the longest 52-week paper rose 0.03 percent to 19.46 percent against the secondary quotings at 19.41/19.37 percent at 0115 GMT, and the maximum yield was 0.01 up to 19.47 percent.

Dealers said banks have curbed investment at the NBP's operations this month so as to avoid a rate surge at the end of the month like in late September. The trade was balanced on Monday amid slight overliquidity.
One-day rates eased slightly, but some traders said they might rise on Tuesday on monthly tax payments.

"I expect the main impact of the taxes tomorrow," said Maciej Ratulowski from Bank Zachodni SA. At 1205 GMT O/N deposits were quoted at 18.65/18.90 percent against opening's 18.80/19.10 percent. T/N were at 18.85/19.10 percent from 18.80/19.25 percent. -- Krzysztof Wojcik +48 22 653 9700
